question: Why did Marie Curie name the element polonium after Poland?
answer: To make a point. In 1898 Poland, where she was born, did not exist as a country: it had been divided between Russia, Prussia and Austria. Naming a new element after it was a protest, and polonium became the first element named to make a political point.
move: Even scientific names can carry a political message.
simply: Marie Curie's country had been wiped off the map by its neighbours. She named a new element after it so the world would remember Poland.
why: Names shape memory. Noticing who chose a name, and why, often reveals history hiding in plain sight, in streets, places and even elements.
reference: Sam Kean, The Disappearing Spoon (Little, Brown, 2010), ch. 12
